newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S GAUTENG RECEIVES 23 CASINO LICENCE BIDS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S GAUTENG RECEIVES 23 CASINO LICENCE BIDS.

text.p: The gambling and betting board of South Africa's Gauteng province said on Thursday it had received 23 applications for its six casino licences.

Legislation passed last year legalised casino gaming in South Africa for the first time and gave control of the running of the industry to the country's nine provinces. Gauteng, the most populous province, is allowed to award the greatest number of licences.

Included on the list of applicants is black empowerment group MoAfrika Casino Holdings which on Wednesday unveiled plans to build a 2.5 billion rand retail and leisure centre in the next three years. It said it planned to add a casino to the complex.

Tsogo Sun Holdings, a joint-venture between a black consortium and South African Breweries hotels unit Southern Sun and which has already secured two licences in Mpumalanga province, submitted two bids.
The Global Resorts Consortium, which secured the third Mpumulanga licence awarded, has submitted one Gauteng bid.

Johnnic Casino Holdings Ltd had made application to to build a casino at Gallagher Estate in the Midrand area outside Johannesburg, while Stocks Leisure Holdings Ltd was looking at the neighbouring Centurion area.
Afrisun Gauteng, part of the Sun International South Africa Ltd grouping and Karos Hospitality/Karos Leisure had also applied.

Other bids for the Gauteng licences came from Crestalia Gaming, Ryoct Investments, Silver Star Development, Rhino Heltel & Resort, City Urban Renewal Enterprises, Carlton Centre and Carlton Legend, Soweto Investments, Akani Egoli, Green Oaks Trading and Letsha La Pula.
